excerpts: **Geno bounces back.** It's been a rough couple of weeks for the Jets and especially painful (quite literally) for [Geno Smith](https://www.nfl.com/players/geno-smith) , who has been under constant duress and taken more than his fair share of hits from opposing defenses amid the Jets' struggles. Sunday represented a respite. Smith was sharp and seemed to play with a sense of empowerment, making plays in and out of structure to help the Jets capitalize on a couple of 70-yard scoring marches. He was efficient, too -- which was especially important in a game that saw a total of 12 possessions and took just two hours and 40 minutes from start to finish -- completing 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards, three touchdowns and a passer rating of 141.2. It helps, of course, when a quarterback's ball carriers run 36 times for 161 yards, and it's also nice when a veteran elevated from the practice squad, [Sterling Shepard](https://www.nfl.com/players/sterling-shepard) , rediscovers his ability to find open spaces and make catches amid chaos for two touchdowns. Overall, it was nicest for Jets fans, who have spent too much of the 2026 season watching their Sundays end in disappointment.

**NFL Research:** Geno Smith had his first win with at least three passing touchdowns and no interceptions since his last game for the Seahawks in Week 18, 2025, against the Rams (which was also a win at SoFi Stadium).

excerpts: **Slow-moving Chargers fall in frustrating fashion.** It's Week 11, yet it remains abundantly clear that [Justin Herbert](https://www.nfl.com/players/justin-herbert) trusts very little of this offense, if anything or anyone at all. He's constantly quick to pull his eyes down and search for an escape route after dropping to pass, the element of surprise attached to his legs has disappeared, and the combination has crippled this entire offense. That reality makes for a grind of an offensive experience for Los Angeles, which included some peculiar play calls and generally poor execution. Sunday featured examples for each of these categories. A screen called late in the third quarter only went for a gain of 4 because right guard [Kayode Awosika](https://www.nfl.com/players/kayode-awosika) lollygagged his way through traffic (and was briefly held by a defender) before making a late attempt to get out in front of pass catcher [Omarion Hampton](https://www.nfl.com/players/omarion-hampton) . A fourth-quarter touchdown drive required 16 plays, ate up 7:48 of game clock and required a ticky-tack illegal hands to the face penalty to buy the Chargers an extra set of downs near the goal line before Herbert, who was announced to be in concussion protocol after the game, connected with [Ladd McConkey](https://www.nfl.com/players/ladd-mcconkey) for his [second score of the day.](https://www.nfl.com/videos/justin-herbert-locates-ladd-mcconkey-for-his-second-td-late-in-the-fourth) On that same drive, facing third-and-2 from the Jets' 43 in a 10-point game with seven minutes left in regulation, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel dialed up a flea-flicker, resulting in a deep incompletion. It's a call you make when you know you're going for it on fourth down, but for an offense that finished with 261 yards in a low-possession contest, it was an odd-at-best choice if not entirely inexplicable, and the ensuing down required Jets rookie cornerback [D'Angelo Ponds](https://www.nfl.com/players/d-angelo-ponds) to give up on a play early to allow [Kimani Vidal](https://www.nfl.com/players/kimani-vidal) to barely cross the line to gain. Later in that drive, McDaniel directed Herbert to run a speed option out of the pistol to the short side of the field on first-and-goal from the Jets' 8. Yes, he called for a quarterback who had been hit all afternoon (he was sacked six times) to run an option toward the boundary, inside the final four minutes of a 10-point game. All of this is to express one overarching point: This team is incredibly frustrating to watch and seemingly unaware of why that's the case. Their nickname is Chargers -- represented by a lightning bolt, which is known to strike incredibly quickly -- but their pace is more fitting of a glacier.

recap.paragraph: Geno Smith zips a 16-yard touchdown pass to Sterling Shepard! It is Shepard’s second touchdown catch of the game. Breece Hall also grabs a touchdown pass from Smith. Justin Herbert runs for a Chargers touchdown and later finds Ladd McConkey for another. The Jets hold on for a thrilling 27-24 win in Los Angeles! They end a 5-game skid and improve to 3-8, while the Chargers fall to 1-9.
